page: Google Cloud Platform n1-highcpu-8 is a compute-skewed virtual machine instance from the N1 machine series. Powered by Intel Xeon x86_64 processors running at a base clock of 2.3 GHz, it provides 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical execution cores via hyper-threading. The system configuration is provisioned with 7.0 GB of total RAM, translating to an allocation of roughly 0.9 GB per vCPU. The instance includes no integrated local NVMe storage and no GPU hardware accelerators, necessitating network-attached storage volumes for file systems and disk persistence.

Benchmark measurements indicate processing performance characteristic of older generation cloud infrastructure. The instance recorded a Geekbench single-core score of 914.0 and a multi-core score of 3557.0, alongside stress-ng results of 1109.79 for single-core and 5820.12 for multi-core compute. In PassMark testing, the CPU achieved an overall score of 6786.78. Memory bandwidth shows moderate capability on large data transfers, achieving 47.28 GB/sec on uncached large-block reads and 34.7 GB/sec on writes, though smaller cached read transfers and compression tasks such as single-threaded gzip show weaker relative throughput.

The constrained memory footprint of 7.0 GB establishes a distinct resource tradeoff, restricting deployment to jobs that do not maintain sizable in-memory data structures. Without newer instruction set extensions such as AVX-512, heavy matrix operations and modern vector calculations remain limited. Within these parameters, the n1-highcpu-8 offers practical utility for CPU-intensive parallel worker queues, distributed compilation nodes, continuous integration runners, and light batch-processing tasks where vCPU count is prioritized over memory capacity.
description: Google Cloud Platform n1-highcpu-8 is an x86_64 compute-oriented virtual machine configuration featuring 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical Intel Xeon cores at 2.3 GHz. Equipped with 7.0 GB of system memory, the instance offers a low memory allocation of approximately 0.9 GB per vCPU, without bundled local storage or GPU hardware. In benchmark tests, the legacy architecture delivers modest processing performance, recording a Geekbench multi-core score of 3557.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 6786.78. Memory bandwidth yields average large-block sequential read and write speeds of 47.28 GB/sec and 34.7 GB/sec, respectively, though single-core execution and compression workloads exhibit lower efficiency. The absence of modern vector extensions such as AVX-512 further characterizes its compute profile. Consequently, n1-highcpu-8 is practical for cost-conscious, multi-threaded batch workloads, compile pipelines, and lightweight CPU-bound microservices that do not require extensive memory footprints or massive per-core instruction throughput.
